label: <DEL> step of long (L=8-9) sequences with t among the first three tokens
explanation: Fires only on the <DEL> delimiter step (100% of activation mass), and only for long sequences: L=9 (83% of mass) and L=8 (17%). It never fires in the original or copy phases or for L<=7. Even there it is rare (about 2% of L=9 delimiter steps), and which sequences trigger it depends on content spread over the whole sequence. Early tokens matter most: t in positions 0-2 (lift up to ~22x for t at position 1), g or t as the first token, and j/p/k/o/r as the second token. A final token of e/b/j/u also helps. The strongest activations come from sequences that open with t/g followed by t/j and end in e/b. The predicate captures ~70% of mass but its precision is low (~8%), because most long sequences with an early t do not cross the threshold. It looks like the tail of a distributed readout of the sequence contents, not a clean token detector.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=t (+2.81), prev_tok=e (+2.64), orig2=t (+2.62), phase=1 & out_tok=g (+2.60), next_out=j (+2.57), next_out=t (+2.31). Lower it: orig7=- (-5.26), in_first=0 (-4.63), in_count=1 (-2.12), orig2=0 (-2.08).
